mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of Panama and licensed Panamanian bank or fiduciary institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, foundation council members, beneficiaries, protector, representative, and registered agent against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panamanian national sanctions and terrorism-financing lists. Enhanced due diligence applies to foreign and domestic Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates in strict compliance with Ley No. 23 de 2015, Executive Decree No. 363 de 2019, and FATF Recommendation 12. Continuous risk-based monitoring must be performed at inception and throughout the foundation's lifecycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Portal Electrónico del Registro Público de Panamá (Sistema de Reserva de Nombre del Registro Público)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Filings must be conducted in Spanish. Foreign-language foundation names are permitted when written in Latin script; non-Latin script names require a sworn Spanish transliteration or certified translation. The foundation name must include the mandatory suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or related statutory indicator and must be clearly distinguishable from existing registrations after application of token-matching and phonetic-equivalence rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is rejected, the applicant or registered agent may file a written recurso de reconsideración before the Director General del Registro Público within five business days of notice, attaching a corrective alternative name. If the reconsideration is denied, an apelación under Panama's administrative litigation rules may be submitted to the Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within fifteen business days, requesting judicial review of the registry's administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are permissible for the administrative seat and back-office operations of the Private Interest Foundation, but the marine insurance surveying licensed business must maintain a substantive physical presence or otherwise comply with any sectoral inspection requirements imposed by the Panamanian maritime and insurance supervisory authorities. A post-office-box-only address does not satisfy commercial substance or registered office obligations for this regulated activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate, with approximately 25% likelihood of a registered-agent compliance inspection within the first 12 months and 15-20% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection of the business premises for a low-risk marine survey operation, rising if UBO verification or updated due diligence is triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), arts. 6, 8, 13-16; complemented by the Panamanian Commerce Code and the Public Registry Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Mercantile Section (Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Personas Jurídicas y Mercantil), Archive of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter and Articles of Establishment (Instrumento Fundacional / Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The foundation's initial endowment must be at least USD 10,000 (no less than this statutory minimum). No escrow or deposit account is required before registration; a notarized declaration of initial capital contribution is sufficient and must be kept in the foundation records.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial foundation capital of USD 10,000 be and is hereby accepted as declared by the Founder; that the registered office be established at [Calle 50, Panama City], and that the law firm [Name] be and is hereby designated as the resident agent; and that [Name], as President, [Name], as Secretary, and [Name], as Treasurer, shall constitute the Foundation Council with full authority to administer the foundation's assets, open banking and custody accounts, execute marine survey contracts, and exercise all powers provided under Ley 25 of 1995; and that the Secretary be authorised to publish the required notice in the Gaceta Oficial and to file all necessary registrations with the Public Registry of Panama.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Foundation Charter and Initial Capital Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama (Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Foundation Charter (Instrumento Fundacional) in Spanish, including the foundation name, statement of initial endowment of at least USD 10,000, registered office in Panama, founding council members, and the marine cargo survey purpose. Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney to review the draft. Execute and notarize the charter and the capital declaration before a Panamanian Notary. Retain a certified Spanish translation of any foreign-language source documents.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter in Spanish
Notarized Initial Endowment Declaration (USD 10,000 minimum)
Certified copy of founder's valid passport
Proof of source of funds for the endowment
Attorney engagement letter and notarial fees receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary questions the endowment valuation or the purpose clause, file a corrective addendum (Adenda) to the charter for re-notarization before the same or another Notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Mercantile Section (Registro Público de Panamá, Sección de Personas Jurídicas y Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the fully notarized Foundation Charter and all supporting annexes with the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry. Complete the official application form, pay the applicable registration fee (USD 350 approximate), and obtain a date-stamped filing receipt. The filing must be presented by the Panamanian resident agent or a licensed attorney.
required_dossiers: Signed and notarized Foundation Charter and annexes
Payment receipt for the public registry registration fee
Duly authenticated power of attorney of the resident agent or attorney
Filing application form of the Registro Público
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises a name conflict, defective documentation, or missing signature, submit a 'Memorial' (written brief) requesting correction or an amendment deed within 8 business days. Re-file upon curing the stated defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Foundation Excerpt in the Official Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: La Gaceta Oficial de Panamá (Official Gazette of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, prepare and submit a certified excerpt (extracto) of the Foundation Charter to the Official Gazette for mandatory publication. The excerpt must state the foundation name, date of execution, and registry registration number. Arrange payment of the publication fee and obtain the printed page of the Gazette as public notice.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Foundation Charter
Official application for publication in the Gaceta Oficial
Payment receipt for the Gaceta publication service
Copy of the registration filing receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, request expedited publication and submit the paid filing receipt to any third party requiring legal proof. A certificate of publication can be requested from the Gaceta Oficial to resolve inquiries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Certified Registration Certificate and Foundation Council Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Certificates Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the foundation is duly registered and published, request from the Certificates Department a Certified Registration Certificate (Certificado de Registro) evidencing the foundation's existence, registered address, and Council members. Simultaneously obtain an authenticated copy of the registered foundation appointments to confirm the President, Secretary, and Treasurer in office.
required_dossiers: Original filing number assigned by the Public Registry
Payment receipt for the certificate issuance fee
Valid identification of the resident agent or attorney making the request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors in the foundation name or councilors, file a written correction request with the appropriate Registry branch. If a councilor refuses the appointment, convene a extraordinary foundation council meeting to ratify a substitute councilor and record the resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Foundation Council Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: PA_PIF – Foundation Council and Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the inaugural meeting of the Foundation Council and adopt the first resolution as set out in the pro-forma text. Execute the minutes and acceptance letters. Maintain the statutory books: foundation minutes, register of beneficiaries, and the registered office record. The resident agent must retain a certified copy of the charter and capital declaration for client files.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution (minutes of the foundation council)
Signed acceptance letters from each council member
Register of beneficiaries
Certified copy of the published Gaceta excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If governance documentation is incomplete or inconsistent with the registry record, adopt a ratification resolution or amend the charter via a private instrument filed with the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License and Marine Survey Industrial Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama – Office of Tax Administration and the Panama Maritime Authority (Autoridad Marítima de Panamá); subject to insurance adjuster licensing by the Superintendency of Insurance and Reinsurance of Panama (SSRP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an Aviso de Operación request with the Municipality of Panama for the professional service activity 'marine insurance survey'. Obtain the municipal patent (tax) for the registered office address. For the marine survey activity itself, apply with the Panama Maritime Authority for authorization as a marine claims surveyor. In addition, if the company will act as an appointed adjuster for insurance carriers, obtain the relevant adjuster license with the SSRP under the insurance regulation framework. Provide proof of office location, fire clearance, and professional liability insurance.
required_dossiers: Completed Aviso de Operación form (Spanish)
Certified Registration Certificate of the foundation
Municipal patent fee receipt
Fire safety inspection certificate issued by SINAPROC
Structural occupancy declaration for the office premises
Professional liability insurance policy (marine survey practice)
SSRP license application and fingerprinting forms (if adjuster role is undertaken)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality rejects the activity code, resubmit using the ISIC 5222 classification with a letter from the resident agent. If the Panama Maritime Authority or SSRP raises objections, provide supplementary academic, professional, and insurance-related qualifications; appeal to the relevant appellate administrative chamber within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Panama Maritime Authority (Autoridad Marítima de Panamá – AMP) and Superintendency of Insurance and Reinsurance of Panama (Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panamá – SSRP)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Claims Surveyor Operating License (Licencia de Ajustador de Seguros Marítimos / Autorización de Perito Marítimo) and local Municipal Patent (Aviso de Operación)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Ministerio de Ambiente – MiAMBIENTE), National Directorate of Environmental Risks
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Low Impact – Administrative Registration). Full EIA Report not required for professional marine survey office activities with no industrial processing or hazardous emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater discharges must comply with MiAMBIENTE regulations under Executive Decree 27 of 2014 and the National Discharge Standards (Causas de Contaminación del Agua). Air emissions are limited to emergency standby generators, if any, requiring maintenance and calibration to avoid exceedance of the Panamanian ambient air quality standards. Solid waste and used paper must be handled through authorized municipal collection, with no VOC-emitting industrial processes permitted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the National Civil Protection Service (SINAPROC), structural load inspection for the office premises verified by the Municipality of Panama, and occupational health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Labor and Labor Development (MITRADEL) under the General Regulation for Occupational Safety and Health.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; electronic portal: SICE (Sistema de Información de Control de la Facturación Electrónica)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity acting as a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must appoint a resident agent and obtain an Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT) by filing the corresponding registration form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyente) with the DGI. The resident agent submits the foundation charter, appointment documents, and proof of the registered office. A separate municipal license (Aviso de Operación) is required for local business operations, although a PIF with no Panamanian-source income remains registrable for ITBMS compliance when importing taxable services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a check-the-box entity classification system comparable to the U.S. or a full hybrid mismatch election regime. A PIF is a legal person sui generis under the Private Interest Foundations Law (Law 25 of 1995); it is not classified as a corporation or trust for Panamanian tax purposes. No elective pass-through status exists. For cross-border purposes, the PIF may be characterized per the applicable foreign tax law; Panama law does not provide an entity-level election that would alter its territorial-source taxation status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios, ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All persons performing taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama must register with the DGI. A special small-taxpayer regime applies to individuals and entities with annual gross receipts not exceeding B/.36,000 (equivalent to US$36,000), allowing an optional simplified flat-tax scheme instead of standard ITBMS registration. Non-resident digital and cross-border service suppliers without a local permanent establishment are required to register and charge ITBMS upon the first taxable supply to a Panamanian recipient.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing through the SICE platform is mandatory for all registered taxpayers, including marine insurance surveyors. Invoices must be digitally signed and transmitted using DGI-authorized billing software or the SICE web portal. The DGI validates the invoice series and provides a unique authorization code before issuance; continuous real-time fiscal clearance is not yet implemented, but each invoice requires immediate validation and digital stamping. Failure to comply with invoicing rules may trigger fines and the disallowance of input ITBMS credits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under ITBMS applies to services rendered to non-resident recipients when the benefit of the service is effectively used or consumed outside Panama. Marine insurance surveying services (hull and cargo damage inspection) qualify for the 0% rate when performed on vessels or cargo located outside Panamanian territory, or when the service is supplied to a foreign underwriter with no Panamanian establishment and the survey report is delivered abroad. Supporting documentation must demonstrate that the recipient is a non-resident and that the service is not connected with any Panama-situs asset or local consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (if any physical cargo samples or adjustable equipment are exported from Panama)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (for the movement of any physical items supporting the survey)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Comprobante de Ingreso de Divisas) evidencing receipt of foreign currency within the applicable repatriation period
Duly executed marine survey service contract with the foreign underwriter or charterer
Final survey report and delivery acknowledgment issued to the non-resident client
Commercial invoice bearing the zero-rating legend referencing the ITBMS export exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI audits export zero-rating claims thoroughly. If the documentation requirement is not met or funds are not repatriated within 180 days, the zero-rated supply is retroactively re-characterized as a taxable Panamanian supply. The taxpayer is then liable for the full 7% ITBMS, interest, and surcharges. Fraudulent claims carry administrative fines of up to 100% of the omitted tax, monetary penalties per infraction, and criminal prosecution under Articles 708-B and 793-A of the Fiscal Code for tax fraud, including imprisonment for serious violations. Additionally, the exporter may lose the right to input tax credits and face temporary suspension of invoicing privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — the Republic of Panama maintains no currency-issuing central bank; the US Dollar is legal tender and the Balboa exists solely as a coin-denomination pegged at 1:1 par. The SBP functions as the consolidated banking, foreign-exchange and payments-systems supervisor, while Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the Government's fiscal agent and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) performs AML/CFT financial-intelligence functions. There is no central-bank exchange-control department, no prior-authorization mechanism for capital movements, and no reserve-requirement restriction on foreign-currency deposits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Unrestricted full convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Panama has no exchange-control statute, no conversion licensing, no repatriation quotas, and no remittance impediment for profits, dividends, or foundation distributions to non-resident beneficiaries. Commercial banks record accounts directly in USD, eliminating dual-currency settlement risk for the PIF. Fiscal friction arises only from the territorial tax model: a Private Interest Foundation engaged entirely in offshore marine surveying is exempt from Panamanian corporate income tax on non-source income; Panamanian-source activity would attract the 25% corporate income tax plus a 10% dividend withholding on distributions sourced locally. Survey fees invoiced from shipowners, P&I clubs, and underwriters located outside Panama remain territorial exclusions with zero effective tax, subject to the annual USD 350 operating-license franchise tax, the PIF registration maintenance fees, and accounting-record retention under Law 254 of 2018.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export or cross-border service proceeds. A marine insurance surveyor may retain full USD, GBP, or EUR balances in domestic accounts or sweep them abroad without regulatory approval. Banking counterparties nonetheless apply Law 23 of 2015 AML controls: structured cash transactions exceeding USD 10,000 trigger currency-transaction reports, and all trade invoices must be retained alongside the foundation's registered accounting books to satisfy economic-substance requirements. No SBP or UAF filing is required for the mere crediting of export service fees.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD) — primary revenue collection, disbursement and treasury concentration

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banistmo, S.A. (Grupo Aval / Banco de Bogotá group)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD) — FX forward and cross-currency swap counterparty

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a secondary outbound settlement rail (Wise Business, Mercury, or Currencycloud) for invoices at or below USD 15,000, and Low for primary treasury custody. Legal constraints: offshore digital EMIs hold no Panamanian banking license, no EU EMI passport extends into Panama, and any EMI receiving funds on behalf of the PIF acts only through its US or Belgian licensed banking partner executing MT103-equivalent transfers. Panamanian tier-1 banks will require the foundation's council resolution expressly designating the EMI as an approved disbursement channel; any circulation pattern between the tier-1 account and the EMI triggers enhanced due diligence against shell-sweep typologies. Safest architecture: use Wise solely to collect Lloyd's-market fee remittances, convert GBP/EUR proceeds to USD within Wise, then sweep to Banco General within five banking days.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panamanian law imposes no universal in-person appearance mandate, but every tier-1 bank's compliance committee requires at least one natural-person signatory — a council member, the protector, or an attorney holding a notarized power-of-attorney — to attend an interview, either in a Panama City branch or through compliant video identification coupled with apostilled documents. Fully remote opening for a non-resident PIF is feasible, though onboarding extends from approximately 10 to 35 business days and triggers enhanced non-face-to-face risk weighting. The registered agent, a resident fiduciary, must co-sign the custody mandate and evidence the foundation's good standing. Additional requirements include a fiscal-residence declaration and W-9/Form 3001-equivalent disclosure for every officer and 25%-plus economic beneficiary. Practical recommendation: conduct a single-day Panama City compliance session, notarize council signatures, and thereby eliminate the most burdensome layer of documentary legalization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity of the Private Interest Foundation structure, where beneficiaries are not publicly registered in the Foundation Charter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Non-public Foundation Reglamento containing an express beneficiary list; Registry-issued Certificate of Good Standing; legal opinion from a Panamanian counsel practising under Law 25 of 1995 identifying the founder-settlor, council members, protector and economic beneficiaries; and a signed Beneficial Ownership Declaration submitted to the Registry's EDD portal in accordance with Cabinet Decree 2019-16.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the USD 10,000 statutory endowment and subsequent founder contributions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements on the remitting account; CPA-certified source-of-wealth report; settlor's invoicing trail proving marine-survey or insurance income; warranty deed or custody statement where the endowment is funded in-kind; and a sworn declaration before a Panama Notary attesting the lawful origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived linkage between marine claims surveying and fraudulent loss-inflation or insurance-fraud typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed engagement letters from recognized P&I clubs and hull underwriters; current IIMS (International Institute of Marine Surveying) membership certificate; professional-indemnity insurance policy; a specimen survey report with GPS-stamped and photographic evidence; and a claims-history register demonstrating no contingency-fee arrangement with any claimant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance and accounting-record concerns arising under Law 254 of 2018 for a non-resident-managed PIF.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual attestation filed through the registered agent confirming books retained at the registered office; CPA-prepared financial statements; appointment of a Panama-licensed accountant; and operational evidence comprising vessel call sheets, cargo-inspection timestamps at Cristobal or Balboa anchorage, and digital project logs reconciling survey report numbers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and negative-news hits on counterparties such as cargo owners, freight forwarders, or flagged jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC SDN and EU consolidated-list screening results refreshed within 45 days; Registry Mercantil corporate extracts of counterparties; exact cargo description and voyage origin/destination in each survey mandate; and a counterparty risk-assessment memorandum demonstrating low-risk cargo-insurance relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire-laundering concern from rapid in-and-out sweeps between the tier-1 account and the Wise/offshore EMI channel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy manual establishing a five-business-day EMI holding rule; council resolution approving Underwriter_Wire and Wise as designated clearing rails; monthly treasury reconciliation signed by the appointed accountant; and a pre-approved bank callback protocol for any disbursement above USD 25,000 routed to the EMI.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) the settlor instructs its home bank to transmit SWIFT MT103 (Type 202 cover only where the sending bank lacks direct USD clearing); (2) the beneficiary field must carry the exact foundation legal name, the PIF's account number at Banco General or Global Bank, and the reference 'FCI-E / Law 25 of 1995 — Initial Endowment for Private Interest Foundation under Panama'; (3) the remitter must be the settlor or the corporate founder named in the Charter to preserve source-of-funds traceability; (4) contributions above USD 50,000 require a council resolution and a notarized contribution letter retained with the registered agent; (5) intermediary banks may request a copy of the Foundation Certificate of Incumbency, which should be pre-positioned with executing banks; (6) no exchange-control form or central-bank notification is required, but the DGI must see the credit recorded under 'Patrimonio Inicial' or 'Aportes del Fundador' in the accounting books — never as gross income — to preserve the non-taxable capital nature of the inflow and protect the territorial classification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail mapping by transaction type: — subcontract surveyor fee settlements: SWIFT MT103 direct with purpose code 'SURV — Marine Surveying Fees' and shared-cost instructions; — hull and cargo claim payments when the PIF acts as loss-settlement agent for a P&I club or underwriter: SWIFT MT103 or a UCP600 Commercial Letter of Credit opened by the underwriting bank, payable at sight against presentation of the final signed survey report, the average-adjuster's classification letter, and the claimant's commercial invoice annotated with deductible; — reinsurer premium nets if captive functionality is later added: MT101 multi-customer files or MT202 concentration sweeps to the panel bank's in-house USD account; — domestic cost base covering registry fees, fiscal-agent fees, and accounting retainers: ACH Panama (Sistema de Cámara de Compensación) drawn on the operational account; — Wise secondary rail: invoices below USD 15,000 may be paid through Wise's fast-payment gateway, while any payment above USD 15,000 must be escalated to MT103 for settlement finality. Every outbound transaction must show the PIF as originator and include 'ISIC 5222 Marine Survey' in the reference field for counterparty reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/USD and GBP/USD) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement executed with Banistmo or Banco General as the SBP-licensed counterparty, tenors 1M–12M, used to hedge UK P&I club and Lloyd's-market fee receivables.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) against USD for exotic-liquidity currencies (MXN, COP, PHP) where cargo-premium flows originate in jurisdictions without deliverable local markets; executed OTC with an international licensed bank; no central-bank pre-clearance applicable.
Cross-Currency Swaps (GBP/USD and EUR/USD) converting underwriting-fee streams into the USD/Balboa operating currency, documented under an ISDA Credit Support Annex with collateral postings in USD.

Vanilla FX Options (plain call/put EURUSD and GBPUSD) purchased from the panel bank to hedge contingent claim-pool payments where claim quantum is uncertain; premium paid in advance; exotic and barrier instruments prohibited by internal treasury policy.

Non-Deliverable Swaps (NDS) for tenor-matched reinsurance premium flows (12M–24M) where the PIF executes back-to-back settlement agreements with cedent insurers, with periodic USD fixings referencing WM/Refinitiv rates at noon New York time.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Fee (Tasa Única Anual; Aviso de Operación exemption)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Registro Público de Panamá via Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before September 30 of each calendar year (fixed public deadline, not anniversary-based)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers statutory interest of 1% per month on the unpaid fee plus a 10% surcharge for the first month of delay; persistent non-payment for more than 12 months results in loss of good standing, refusal of certificates of existence, and final administrative strike-off/dissolution by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and Record Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI and UAF (Financial Analysis Unit) inspection-ready files maintained by the Registered Agent; no public filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the PIF's anniversary date each year; within 30 days of any change in Foundation Council members, beneficiaries, or protector direction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Law 23 of 2015 ranging from USD 5,000 to USD 50,000 per violation for material non-compliance or wilful misdeclaration; repeated violations can trigger suspension of the foundation's registration until the UBO file is rectified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Existencia y Representación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá issued through the Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Applicable immediately after payment of the annual fee; commonly obtained for banking, legal, and counterparty diligence, typically within March–October to support annual compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No statutory filing by itself; however, failure to maintain a current certificate of good standing due to unpaid annual fees will block all notarial instruments, asset transfer registrations, and notarized resolutions; eventual strike-off if the annual fee remains unpaid for two consecutive years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit requirement applies to a Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995. Mandatory independent audit triggers only if the foundation elects to carry on commercial activities in Panama and its annual Panama-source gross revenue exceeds USD 3,000,000, in which case the DGI may require audited financial statements accompanying the corporate income tax return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Panama; simplified IFRS for SMEs is acceptable for foundations not publicly responsible.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 23 of 2015 does not impose a government filing of UBO data; instead the Registered Agent must physically maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register. The Foundation Council supplies a written annual confirmation, by resolution or signed statement, identifying natural persons who directly or indirectly own or control more than 10% of the foundation assets, receive distributions, or exercise control of the charter. The confirmation must be updated within 30 days of any share of beneficial entitlement transfer, council change, or beneficiary redistribution. The register is inspected by the UAF, DGI, or judicial authorities under an existing formal request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (Libro de Miembros del Consejo)
Minute Book of Council Resolutions and Decisions (Libro de Actas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 2,500 per year (includes registered office, registered agent, compliance review, and annual fee administration)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 – USD 5,000 if no audit is triggered; feely negotiated from USD 4,000 for a voluntarily prepared IFRS review or full audit of a low-activity marine surveying enterprise

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (progressive brackets per Law 254 of 2022: 19% on net taxable income up to USD 50,000; 25% from USD 50,001 to USD 1,500,000; 27% on the excess over USD 1,500,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial-source taxation only: all foreign-source marine survey and claims-inspection fees are exempt from Panamanian corporate income tax. No sector-specific tax holiday exists for ISIC 5222; the effective rate is reduced to 19% on the first USD 50,000 bracket, and Panama imposes no domestic withholding tax on interest or royalties paid to non-residents. A Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995 that engages in commercial marine surveying is taxed as an ordinary legal entity on Panama-source income.
